Theorem
[Boundary weak Harnack inequality] 1. ch9:9.27\group chapter-9Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0263 Let $u\in W^{2,n}(\Omega )$ satisfy $Lu\le f$ in $\Omega $ and $u\ge 0$ in $B_{2R}(y)\cap \Omega $. Set \[ m=\inf _{B_{2R}(y)\cap \partial \Omega }u \] and extend the truncation by \[ u_m^-(x)= \begin{cases} \min \{ u(x),m\} ,& x\in B_{2R}(y)\cap \Omega ,\\ m,& x\in B_{2R}(y)\setminus \Omega . \end{cases} \] Then, for constants $p,C>0$ depending only on $n,\gamma ,\nu R^2$, \begin{equation} \tag {9.65} \left(\frac1{|B_R|}\int _{B_R(y)}(u_m^-)^p\right)^{1/p} \le C\left(\inf _{\Omega \cap B_R(y)}u+ \frac R\lambda \| f\| _{L^n(\Omega \cap B_{2R}(y))}\right). \end{equation} If only $u\in W^{2,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ is assumed, replace $m$ by $\liminf _{x\to B_{2R}(y)\cap \partial \Omega }u(x)$.
Proof

\sketch Repeat the proof of Theorem 47 with the extended truncation. The level-set estimate applies up to level $m$, while the distribution function vanishes above $m$. The liminf formulation follows by interior exhaustion.

□
